title: Closed Ruy Lopez
intro: After 5...Be7, White protects e4 with Re1, tucks the bishop away on b3 and c2, plays c3, h3 and d4, and steers the knight towards the kingside.
variation: e2e4 e7e5 g1f3 b8c6 f1b5 a7a6 b5a4 g8f6 e1g1 f8e7

lessons.title: Setting up Re1 and Bb3
lessons.summary: Defend e4, retreat Bb3, then prepare d4 with c3 and h3.

steps.text: In the Closed Ruy Lopez, Black declines the e4 pawn and develops 5...Be7.
Defend e4 and threaten Bxc6 followed by Nxe5.
steps.hint: Put your rook behind the e-pawn.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6.Re1 to guard e4 and activate your rook.
steps.ifRight: Now e5 is genuinely threatened, so Black must defend it.

steps.text: Black breaks the pin with 6...b5 before playing ...d6 or castling.
Keep your Spanish bishop on its active diagonal.
steps.ifWrong: Play 7.Bb3 so the bishop still aims at f7 and stays safe.
steps.ifRight: The bishop stays strong on b3.

steps.text: Build a pawn wall for d4 and open the c2 square for your bishop.
steps.ifWrong: Play 8.c3 to prepare d4 and give the b3 bishop a home on c2.
steps.ifRight: Now White is ready for h3 and d4.

steps.text: Black castles: 8...O-O. Stop ...Bg4 before advancing in the centre.
steps.ifWrong: Play 9.h3 so Black cannot pin your knight with ...Bg4.

feedback.d2d4: 9.d4 lets Black play 9...Bg4, putting awkward pressure on d4. Play 9.h3 first.

lessons.title: Meeting 7...O-O (Anti-Marshall)
lessons.summary: Play 8.h3 or 8.a4 to sidestep the Marshall Attack.

steps.text: If Black plays 7...O-O instead of 7...d6, they are preparing the sharp Marshall Attack with 8...d5 after 8.c3.
Play 8.h3 (or 8.a4) to shut down the Marshall Attack cleanly.
steps.hint: Avoid 8.c3 for one move and play h3 or a4 instead.
steps.ifWrong: Play 8.h3 (or 8.a4) so ...d5 is no longer effective.
steps.ifRight: With c3 not yet played, ...d5 simply loses a pawn after exd5 Nxd5 Nxe5.

feedback.c2c3: 8.c3 allows the sharp Marshall gambit 8...d5. Sidestep it with 8.h3 or 8.a4.

steps.text: After 8.h3, Black usually plays 8...d6 to defend e5.
Now that ...d5 is off the table, prepare d4 with your c-pawn.
steps.ifWrong: Play 9.c3, reaching the normal Closed Ruy Lopez.
steps.ifRight: You get the exact Closed Ruy Lopez you wanted without facing the Marshall.

steps.text: If Black answers 8.h3 with 8...Bb7, defend e4 calmly and prepare c3 and d4.
steps.hint: Support e4 with d3 or prepare d4 with c3.
steps.ifRight: White stays solid and plans Nbd2, Nf1 and Ng3.

steps.text: What if Black plays 8...d5 anyway against 8.h3?
steps.ifWrong: Play 9.exd5: after 9...Nxd5 10.Nxe5, White wins a clean central pawn.
steps.ifRight: White simply takes the free pawn.

lessons.title: Meeting 4...b5 and ...Na5
lessons.summary: Ignore the early knight chase and castle into a lead in development.

steps.text: Black sometimes pushes 4...b5 immediately, trying to win your Spanish bishop with ...Na5.
Drop the bishop back to its safe square.
Black jumps in with 5...Na5, attacking the bishop.
Ignore the threat for a moment and castle.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6.O-O: if Black takes on b3, axb3 opens the a-file and you keep a big lead in development.
steps.ifRight: White is ready to strike in the centre with d4.

feedback.b3f7: 6.Bxf7+ Kxf7 7.Nxe5+ Ke8 only helps Black after ...Qe7. Castle calmly with 6.O-O.

steps.text: If Black takes the bishop with 6...Nxb3:
Recapture and activate your a1 rook.
steps.ifWrong: Play 7.axb3 to open the a-file and prepare d4.
steps.ifRight: White leads in development and pushes d4 next.
